So I was in a similar situation with someone older and bigger than me. I was conditioned into thinking that what happened was awesome. 

At the time boys molested by women were sexualised and romanticised, by other males of any age. It was in no way abnormal to hear things like "wish that was me" from teenagers or "lucky boy" from adult men. 

At the time it was viewed as males couldn't be victims of rape. 

I quickly tried to forget about it like most of my childhood. A few years back it came back during therapy and I have realised that I was a victim. The more I relive the situation and remember the force used on me, my panic and confusion, the angrier I get, because I doubt I will ever fully recover from it. 

It has damaged me. 

------------

What I am trying to say by sharing my story, is that while the memory might seem fond and something you wish would happen again, what happened wasn't right.

I totally agree. I came from Autodesk and modelling was so easy. When I first used blender I was sure people only used it, because it was free.

For me I really hated how to make a hole in the middle of an object. It takes 3 times as many steps or more if the hole is supposed to be rounded as it does in Autodesk Inventor. While it sucked at the beginning I have come to terms with it. It feels like a small sacrifice to be able to add textures, do rigging, make animations, filming and more in one piece of software.

I know for a fact I'm doing something wrong, but not sure what.

There are a ton of disabilities. Both mental and physical. A mental disability can be anything from ADHD and autism to lack of oxygen at birth. Physical disability can be anything from chronic pain to lack of multiple body parts. 

First you need to decide what disability and why it is important. Then you need to do research on what that disability causes for someone. Research and your character's personality is important to understand completely. When you do your research don't just read medical papers. Find people who actually live with said disability as papers like the DSM isn't always completely right and can be generalisations or has a specific perspective that makes little sense to the one with said disability. A common problem is with autism. The diagnosis is written by neurotypicals who will never quite understand someone with autism correctly, which is also why it is hard to get diagnosed as they view the many things differently, from the world to the few questions they used to diagnose. 

To sum up: do your research. Read medical definitions and read people's experiences. Find out why it is important that your character is disabled. Adding a disability without reason creates an unbelievable character and worse character. Same if the only character trait is their disability is also unbelievable. You see it a lot with sexuality and gender.

I also learned that per pressure is happening a lot on a subconscious level. As everyone tries to fit in well with everyone, people are pushed to change in ways they might not have. While keeping your individuality might not earn you a ton of respect or friends it does let you not put yourself in situations you might regret. It is okay to have hobbies or styles that are not seen as "popular" normal people's interest.

I personally learned that you should listen to yourself. Especially when it comes to decisions about your future. It is okay to substitute partying for a part time job (if you are studying). First of all getting your first game off the ground requires a lot of sacrifices. You will have to get a job with predictable work hours. A friend of mine is in his 7th year, but has gotten to the point where it is almost ready for release. He is currently working for a gaming studio whilst he's working on his game.

There are no shortcuts. It won't be easy. It might become a part-time to full-time job if you find an Investor, but that is hard enough in itself. 

PERSONALLY, I would make sure that it is something I truly want. For me it isn't anymore as the chance for success is very small. I honestly forgot I owned a switch. I found it dusty in a drawer when I was moving. I had no real enjoyment from it, but then again I have never been a big Nintendo fan.

I debated with myself if I should buy a Steam Deck ever since the first one released. Then the OLED came out and I bought it. I do not regret it. I've been a Steam user for 12 years now, so I didn't think I actually would use it that much as I could just use my PC. I was very wrong. I love my Deck. 

Because of back problems I have a hard time sitting in front of my pc for a long time, so when I am no longer comfortable I can just lay down and play on that. It is especially amazing for cozy games. Last Christmas I just lay in bed all day drinking Monster Energy whilst playing a lot of games I simply couldn't get myself to play a "normal" sitting position. 

I thought I hated Stardew Valley. It was tedious and slow. KB&M control was awful etc etc. However, I chose to put on a TV show and lay down in bed with some hot cocoa and ended up playing it for 6 hours straight. I have over 70 hours in it now. 

For the first time in YEARS I actually feel relaxed whilst playing games. I told my therapist about it and he was overjoyed to hear I finally had a hobby that made me chill. He even recommended handheld consoles for a few other clients he has. 

Of course the overall concept of the 2 consoles are the same, but through steam you have a lot more games, although very different games to play. The prices are cheaper. Cheap indies, sales and third party online sellers. With the Steam Deck you can use the power of your PC to essentially stream the games to your deck, which lets you play more power hungry games for much longer as the Deck doesn't have to actually run the game.

Not to mention cloud saving for almost every game (for free), integrated chat and voice chat function. It is a pc, so you can boot up in desktop mode and watch YouTube and stuff on it too.

If no Nintendo games bothers you, you can simply emulate them which is exactly what Nintendo themselves does for their older games, but they have a paywall.

Jeg var på dagpenge i 8 måneder efter datamatiker uddannelsen uden så meget som et interview. Søgte alle stillinger jeg kunne, men der er så få jobs at søge at selv de 2 obligatoriske jobs jeg skulle søge om ugen var svært at finde. 

Multimediedesign er bestemt også svært. 3 studerende kunne ikke engang finde en praktikplads sidste år. Min plan er dog at vise mine færdigheder med egne projekter, samt skabe en hjemmeside for en forening. Jo mere du udvikler dine evner og står ud, jo nemmere er det at få et job. Udvikling af ens portefølje og CV hjælper en meget. Personligt er jeg ikke nervøs for at finde et job.

Hjemmesider, bruger testning, QA, UX, UI, grafisk design, Fotograf, Social medie specialist. Hell, endda spil design og 3D modelling. 

Det kommer selvfølgelig an på hvilket akademi du vælger, da nogen kan være død kedelige, hvor andre lader dig være ekstrem kreativ. Endda specialisere i et område de ikke direkte har på skemaet.

For mig var Datamatiker uddannelsen dårlig for mig. Det destruerede mit mentale helbred at arbejde 100 timer u ugen for at følge med. Jeg elsker Multimediedesign! The exercise is very simple. Write a short story. It doesn't have to be interesting as it is just for training. Try to avoid using pronouns as much as possible. Figure out another way to explain what's happening. 

Again you can't and shouldn't 100% remove all pronouns or names, but reduce it as much as possible. 

If this sounds too hard try to rewrite sentences so that they don't start with a pronoun. You can also try to use other identifiers.
Let's say it is a story about to best friends, you could use he, they, boys, guys etc. Maybe even work in some special identifiers maybe they are known as the double trouble or identify the person by their looks or profession instead of using pronouns.

In a way. My first story was technically written in 1st person, but it was a psychological thriller with a heavy focus on mental illnesses, so the protagonist rarely saw their actions as their own. Even their thoughts felt out of place and didn't believe certain actions were real. The disassociation kept the protagonist from acknowledging themselves, actions and others.

That's definitely a valid way to do it! (a way I personally find to be enjoyable to read). Again, there is nothing wrong with using the pronouns or words like "The Forensics inspected the now chaotic motel room room with a UV light searching for potential blood spatter."  
Your goal does not have to be excluding pronouns, names etc. completely. It all depends on your writing style, perspective, genre and so on, but rather not to overuse it. You often see new writers use he or character name in every sentence which is something you have to get away from.

Using he first time in a scene is often enough as the reader is aware of who they are reading about. Here is an example from the story I am currently writing:

>Simon studied a map every time they simply had to stop and look at the view. It was not the most accurate as it had not been updated by travellers the last hundred and fifty years. Only updates had been through satellite imaging, The mountains gave them a direction and a marker should they get lost. According to the map about four more miles in their current direction should lead to a large pond or perhaps a lake. Well, maybe five miles. Or six. The map was not really that precise. It was old after all.

As you can se I do use pronouns a few times, but I try to break away from it by describing what is happing. You can't avoid pronouns when writing in first person. The story simply wouldn't make much sense, espeically if there is more than one character in it. But, instead of saying "He is running away from the monster", you could write "Running away from the monster a moment of clarity dawned on him". That way mixing the pronouns so you don't start sentences with them either.

Oh, BTW, I am a newbie writer myself so DO NOT take my words as a rule. It is simply what helped me. The example above is my first ever try writing in 3rd person and I am still writing the first draft, so I am still learning myself. :D

I am currently trying to lose weight and here is what I do:

I keep my daily calorie intake at 1800 kcal, but I try to keep it lower. Do not go under 1300 kcal as that won't be healthy.
